text:
Asha (People Ops): Quick — outpatient ortho clinic in Amsterdam wants Redwood to direct-bill for a splint. They requested payment to a local IBAN and asked for an EOB that hides patient street address. Claim 2026-NL-7721. Who owns the flow and what docs do we need?

Ben (Benefits): Benefits handles coverage. Need signed AOB from member, itemized invoice with local procedure codes and service date, and clinical note supporting medical necessity. We can redact street address with member consent but must keep service dates and codes.

Omar (Finance): For SEPA payment: IBAN + BIC, beneficiary name exactly as bank record, and proof of account (bank letter or screenshot). If invoice includes VAT show VAT line. SEPA normally 1-3 business days after KYC.

Asha (People Ops): Can someone paste a one-paragraph provider email/checklist I can forward?

Ben (Benefits): Paste: "To billing@clinic.nl — please provide: 1) Signed Assignment of Benefits (PDF) for Claim 2026-NL-7721; 2) Itemized invoice in EUR with procedure codes, service date, VAT line if applicable; 3) Clinical note supporting medical necessity; 4) Banking details: IBAN, BIC, account holder name, and proof of account; 5) Billing contact. Send to claims@redwood.com."

ClaimsBot: Automated: International direct-bill triggered. Manual review required; estimated adjudication 4-8 business days after complete docs received.

Asha (People Ops): Thanks — I'll send this. One last: clinic asked if we can send EOB to patient with only initials instead of full name. Allowed?

Ben (Benefits): Only if member signs consent permitting initials-only; otherwise include full name on member-facing EOB. Keep full record internally for audit.

Asha (People Ops): Great, forwarding now. Will update thread when provider replies. :white_check_mark:
